### problem_chain

Walked from the root problem using the policy and the world alone.

**Root.** The customer asks for his badge to charge lunch to payroll again. The only policy in the charter
whose result is that state is `meal_ext_restriction_lift_balance` (`subject: [meal_account_reinstated]`,
base event `mutation: {transition: {from: restricted, to: active}}`; base `meal_restriction_terms`: "A
restricted account keeps its stored value and its allowance and may go on eating; only the payroll tender is
withdrawn"). Its rule carries two prerequisite sentences.

**Edge L→R** — "The charges an account carries forward at reinstatement are fixed only after the charges
awaiting recovery stand net of the recovery entry due for each closed payroll period."
*False at the opening?* Yes. Charges accrued carry seven distinct pay periods; recovery entries exist for
two of them:

| pay_period | charge accrued (posted) | recovery entry |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2025-12-P1 | 52.40 (2025-12-09) | — |
| 2025-12-P2 | 47.85 (2025-12-23) | 100.25 (2026-01-09) |
| 2026-01-P1 | 58.30 (2026-01-14) | — |
| 2026-01-P2 | 44.90 (2026-01-28) | 103.20 (2026-02-06) |
| 2026-02-P1 | 61.75 (2026-02-11) | — |
| 2026-02-P2 | 49.60 (2026-02-25) | — |
| 2026-03-P1 | 56.20 + 43.35 + 38.90 (2026-03-04/10/13) | — |

Which write brings the state about: only `meal_ext_period_recovery_amount` describes booking a recovery
entry (`post_payroll_recovery_c9e76aa9`, `transaction_code="payroll_deduction"`). *Kind* `value_input` on
`balance_standing_usd` ✓.

**Edge L→P** — "The charges carried forward are worked out only once the stored value standing on the
account has been raised by the paydown the plan calls for."
*False at the opening?* Yes: the latest `account_load` row is 2026-01-20 (48.20); no load stands within the
calendar month before `frozen_time`, so `value_loaded_1m = 0.00`. The write is
`load_arrears_paydown_ff1c695b` (`meal_ext_reinstatement_paydown`), the only write that raises
`meal_balance_usd` by a paid-in amount. *Kind* `value_input` on `applied_from_value_usd` ✓.

**Edge P→R** — "The paydown the employee is asked for is not worked out before the charges awaiting
recovery on the account stand net of the recovery entry owed for every closed payroll period." Same state,
same resolving write; *kind* `value_input` on `measured_balance_usd` ✓.

Derived tree (identical in shape to what the author declared, with the strength caveat of CG-3):

```
meal_ext_restriction_lift_balance   (root; agent write)
 ├── value_input ──> meal_ext_reinstatement_paydown       (owner=user write)
 │                    └── value_input ──> meal_ext_period_recovery_amount
 └── value_input ──> meal_ext_period_recovery_amount      (agent write)
```

- nodes 3, prerequisite problems n = 2, edges 3, all `value_input`; floor max(n−1,1) = 1 ✓
- acyclic ✓; topological order: `post_payroll_recovery_c9e76aa9` → `load_arrears_paydown_ff1c695b` →
  `lift_meal_account_restriction_a306574a`
- at least one problem is the customer's own write: `load_arrears_paydown_ff1c695b`, `@tool(owner="user")`,
  "It is your own payment: nobody else may make it for you." The persona hands it over passively: "When the
  agent hands him the means to make that payment and gives him a figure, he repeats the figure back and then
  makes the payment there and then for exactly that amount." ✓
- **parallel edges** — the two out-edges of the root both bear on the same quantity chain, and the order is
  pinned exclusively: `meal_ext_reinstatement_paydown` itself depends on `meal_ext_period_recovery_amount`,
  so recovery-before-paydown is forced by the graph, not chosen. No second order exists.
- **no-wait** — see check 5 above and F-2.

sentence, step 1 is a wait — F-2.) No POLICY_NOT_COVERED route applies: the request is a reinstatement,
which `meal_restriction_terms` and `meal_ext_restriction_lift_balance` cover.

**Object.** `meal_accounts.bfc789e2-5b2b-4e6d-b38a-8c8285a56450`, the only meal account of
`customers.0f2296e6-…` (Theo Vandeleur), `variant_name = "Payroll Deduction Meal Account"`,
`status = "restricted"`, `restriction_start_date = "2026-02-24"`, `site_code = "CS-517"`,

to do whatever it needs to on its own side without checking with him line by line") and the mode for the one

issues no second item of work, and closes exactly where the last gold action closes ("Once he hears that the
account has been put back to normal … he thanks the agent … and rings off"). ✓

## findings

### F-1 — `SOURCE-CHAIN RED` — the prerequisite's condition is still false after the write that is supposed to resolve it

- **symptom** both edges into `meal_ext_period_recovery_amount` wait on a state quantified over **every /
  each** closed payroll period, while the single prescribed write settles one period.
- **root cause** charter-global **CG-3** (`_difficulty.md`, `### findings`); demonstrated here against this
  world.
- **evidence** (this world) charges stand accrued under seven pay periods; recovery entries exist for two:

  | period | charge accrued | recovery entry on the ledger |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | 2025-12-P1 | 52.40 | **none** |
  | 2025-12-P2 | 47.85 | 100.25 (2026-01-09) |
  | 2026-01-P1 | 58.30 | **none** |
  | 2026-01-P2 | 44.90 | 103.20 (2026-02-06) |
  | 2026-02-P1 | 61.75 | **none** |
  | 2026-02-P2 | 49.60 | **none** |
  | 2026-03-P1 | 56.20 + 43.35 + 38.90 | **none** |

  The gold write books one entry, `pay_period="2026-03-P1"`. Four closed periods (2025-12-P1, 2026-01-P1,
  2026-02-P1, 2026-02-P2) still carry no recovery entry afterwards, so
  `prerequisite_closure.edges[0].condition` — "**every** closed payroll period on the account carries its
  own recovery entry on the ledger" — is false both before and after. The GT's own proof text compounds it:
  `unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false` names "2026-02-P1, 2026-02-P2 and 2026-03-P1" and omits 2025-12-P1
  and 2026-01-P1, and the field is called `flips_to_true_by`.
- **demonstrated consequence** two readings of the resolving action. Reading A (the gold one): one write,
  85.05 for 2026-03-P1. Reading B (the sentence taken at its stated strength): a recovery entry for each
  closed period that lacks one. Under reading B, `meal_ext_period_recovery_amount`'s own rule fixes the
  amount and the period from the most recent charge, so it cannot even produce the other four figures — the
  agent is left with a condition it cannot close and a policy that describes one write. Either way the
  downstream `measured_balance_usd` and `balance_standing_usd` are not "net of the recovery entry owed for
  every closed payroll period", so the scored 134.51 and 55.44 rest on a state the artifacts say is
  required and do not reach.
- **affected artifact** `meal.extended.yaml`
  (`meal_ext_reinstatement_paydown.prerequisite[0]`, `meal_ext_restriction_lift_balance.prerequisite[0]`
  and the two rule sentences they quote); `tasks/0.json` `prerequisite_closure.edges[0..1]`.
- **relation to previous revisions** first revision.

### F-2 — `SOURCE-POLICY RED` — base fixes a remittance day that has not arrived; the extended policy acts anyway

- **symptom** step 1 remits the recovery for pay period 2026-03-P1 on 2026-03-17, while the base policy it
  extends says a period's charges are remitted a stated number of days **after the period closes**.
- **root cause** charter-global **CG-4** (`_difficulty.md`); demonstrated here with this plan's lag and
  this task's dates.
- **evidence**
  - base `meal_payroll_recovery_terms`, carried verbatim in `meal.extended.yaml`: "A payroll period's
    charges are remitted **the number of days after the period closes printed against the plan**, and no
    more than the deduction ceiling printed against the same plan is recovered in one period".
  - `meal_ext_period_recovery_amount.overwrite` supersedes only "no more than the deduction ceiling printed
    against the same plan is recovered in one period". The remittance-timing half is inherited in full.
  - the plan: "Payroll Deduction Meal Account", `payroll_deduction_lag_days = 7`.
  - the period: `pay_period` is "YYYY-MM-P followed by one digit **for the half of the month**"
    (`post_payroll_recovery_c9e76aa9` docstring), so 2026-03-P1 closes 2026-03-15; 15 March + 7 = **2026-03-22**.
  - `frozen_time = 2026-03-17 10:35:00 -04:00`.
  - the seeded history honours the lag: 2025-12-P2 (closes 2025-12-31) was remitted 2026-01-09, 2026-01-P2
    (closes 2026-01-31) was remitted 2026-02-06.
- **demonstrated consequence** two answers to now/wait on the same world. Under the inherited base
  sentence the correct answer at `frozen_time` is **wait until 2026-03-22**, which writes nothing today and
  therefore also leaves the paydown and the reinstatement unwritten; under the extended policy's bare
  `trigger: state_due` the answer is act now for 85.05. Nothing in the charter reconciles them, and
  `payroll_deduction_lag_days` appears in no extended rule, no compute binding and no `baseline.params`.
- **affected artifact** `meal.extended.yaml`, `meal_ext_period_recovery_amount.rule` / `.overwrite`; the
  whole of this task's scored solution depends on which reading is taken.
- **relation to previous revisions** first revision.

---

### F-3 — `SOURCE-POLICY RED` — overdraft charges are moved from stored value into payroll arrears with no declaration

- **symptom** step 3 raises the charges awaiting **payroll** recovery by 6.00 of overdraft charges that the
  base charter books against **stored value**, and the displaced base provision is named in no `overwrite`.
- **root cause** charter-global **CG-5** (`_difficulty.md`); demonstrated here.
- **evidence**
  - base event `meal_overdraft_fee_posted`: `account: meal_balance`, `direction: out`.
  - the two rows: `overdraft_fee` 3.00 on 2026-02-13 and 3.00 on 2026-03-09; both are already inside the
    seeded `meal_balance_usd = 8.75` (loads 86.35 + refund 14.25 − purchases 33.45 − guest meals 52.40 −
    overdraft 6.00 = 8.75), which `design_rationale`'s own cache check confirms.
  - extended: `overdraft_carry_usd = overdraft_total_3m` = 6.00, added into `result` with `+`.
  - `meal_ext_restriction_lift_balance.base_policy_refs` names `meal_restriction_terms` and
    `meal_payroll_recovery_terms` only; the event binding and `meal_purchase_and_tender_rules` are named
    nowhere, and `overwrite` names one sentence of `meal_payroll_recovery_terms`.
- **demonstrated consequence** an agent following the base binding carries no overdraft charge into payroll
  arrears and writes **49.44**; the extended policy writes **55.44**. Two defensible answers for the one
  scored parameter, with no declaration to pick between them.
- **affected artifact** `meal.extended.yaml`, `meal_ext_restriction_lift_balance.overwrite`,
  `factors.overdraft_charge_carry`, `compute.overdraft_carry_usd`; scored `arrears_carried_usd`.
- **relation to previous revisions** first revision.

### F-4 — `SOURCE-FACTOR RED` — two tier outcomes charge the employee twice for the same items

- **symptom** `stored_tender_meal_restoration` adds 33.45 — the full value of three meals the employee has
  already paid for out of stored value — into the charges payroll will recover, and
  `overdraft_charge_carry` adds 6.00 of charges already taken out of stored value, with no offsetting
  credit anywhere.
- **root cause** charter-global **CG-6** (`_difficulty.md`); demonstrated here.
- **evidence**
  - the three meals: `meal_purchase` 12.40 (2026-02-27), 9.85 (2026-03-05), 11.20 (2026-03-12), all
    `payment_channel="badge_tap"`. Base event `meal_purchase_posted`: `account: meal_balance`,
    `direction: out` — the stored value has already gone.
  - the two overdraft charges, as in F-3.
  - the target tool `lift_meal_account_restriction_a306574a` updates `status`,
    `restriction_start_date` and `payroll_arrears_usd`; it never touches `meal_balance_usd`. No other
    policy in the charter returns that value.
  - the charter's own account meanings: `meal_balance` = "spendable stored value the employee has on the
    account"; `payroll_arrears` = "meal charges the employee has run up that payroll has not yet
    recovered". These are two distinct pockets of the employee's money.
- **demonstrated consequence** 39.45 of the scored 55.44 — 71 % of the figure — is money the employee has
  already paid, re-billed to their next pay packet. No workplace dining operator publishes that as its
  reinstatement treatment. The factors' fall-through tiers ("nothing is restored", "no overdraft charge is
  carried"), which give 21.99 and 49.44, are what the business does.
- **affected artifact** `meal.extended.yaml`, `meal_ext_restriction_lift_balance` factors
  `stored_tender_meal_restoration` and `overdraft_charge_carry`, their rule sentences and `compute.result`.
- **relation to previous revisions** first revision.

### F-5 — `SOURCE-POLICY RED` — the same refund is relieved twice, because base and extended disagree on where it went

- **symptom** the refund of 14.25 on 2026-02-09 has already raised stored value under the base event
  binding, and step 3 deducts the same 14.25 again from the charges carried forward as a refund "returned
  through payroll".
- **root cause** the base charter contradicts itself about a refund's destination, and the extended policy
  reads one side of the contradiction while the seed reads the other.
- **evidence**
  - base `meal_load_and_refund_terms`: "A refund is returned by the method printed against the plan — to
    stored value, through payroll, or to the card originally used — and never by a method the employee
    chooses on the day." The plan's `refund_method = "to_payroll"`.
  - base event `meal_refund_posted`: `account: meal_balance`, `direction: in` — **unconditionally**, with
    no branch on the plan's method.
  - the seed follows the event binding: `meal_balance_usd = 8.75` only reconciles with the ledger when the
    14.25 is counted **into** stored value (86.35 + 14.25 − 33.45 − 52.40 − 6.00 = 8.75), and
    `design_rationale`'s cache check states exactly that arithmetic.
  - the extended policy follows the plan parameter: `refund_offset_usd = payroll_refunds_3m` gated by
    `P('refund_method') == 'to_payroll'`, subtracted from the carry-forward.
- **demonstrated consequence** the same 14.25 both raises the employee's stored value and reduces what
  payroll will recover. Reading the base event binding as it stands (the refund went to stored value, so
  nothing is set against the arrears) gives **69.69**; the extended reading gives **55.44**. Two
  defensible answers for the scored parameter.
- **affected artifact** `blueprint/products/meal.yaml` and its verbatim copy in `meal.extended.yaml`
  (`events.meal_refund_posted` vs `meal_load_and_refund_terms`), and
  `meal_ext_restriction_lift_balance.factors.payroll_refund_offset`; `initial_state.meal_transactions`
  row `c7237082-…`.
- **relation to previous revisions** first revision.

### F-6 — `SOURCE-CHAIN RED` — the edge's load-bearing proof states a binding value the ladder cannot produce

- **symptom** `prerequisite_closure.edge_load_bearing[2]` and `design_rationale` both assert that with the
  paydown skipped "the value applied from the account is **0.00** and the charges carried forward become
  **189.95**".
- **root cause** the counterfactual was written from the baseline rather than recomputed on the ladder: with
  no load in the month the factor does not fall through to nothing, it takes its **second** rung.
- **evidence**
  - `meal_ext_restriction_lift_balance.factors.value_application_basis` rung 2: "the account stands
    restricted and no value has been loaded onto it in the last calendar month → the halved share of the
    stored value standing"; compute
    `RND(F('meal_balance_usd') * K('half_value_credit_pct') / 100, 2)` with `half_value_credit_pct = 50`.
  - recomputed on the world "recovery posted, paydown skipped": `meal_balance_usd = 8.75`,
    `value_loaded_1m = 0.00` → `applied_from_value_usd = RND(8.75 × 50 %, 2) = **4.38**`, and
    `result = RND(MX(0, 164.75 − 4.38 − 14.25 + 6.00 + 33.45), 2) = **185.57**`.
  - 189.95 is exactly `164.75 − 0.00 − 14.25 + 6.00 + 33.45`, i.e. the figure one gets **only** if
    `applied_from_value_usd` were 0.00 — a value no rung of that ladder yields for a restricted account.
- **demonstrated consequence** the proof the artifact submits for this edge is false as written: it names a
  binding value the charter cannot produce and a result 4.38 away from the recomputation. The edge does
  still bear weight (185.57 ≠ 55.44), so the relationship survives on recomputation — but not on the proof
  offered for it.
- **affected artifact** `tasks/0.json` `prerequisite_closure.edge_load_bearing[2].skipped_effect` and the
  matching line of `design_rationale` ("edge C skipped -> … 189.95 … nothing is applied from the account").
- **relation to previous revisions** first revision.

### F-7 — `SOURCE-CHAIN RED` — the order-uniqueness proof quotes the wrong counterfactual's number

- **symptom** `prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness` asserts that with the paydown placed before the
  recovery "the paydown becomes 150.00 rather than 134.51, and the reinstatement carries **140.49** rather
  than 55.44".
- **root cause** 140.49 is the figure for a *different* counterfactual — skipping the recovery altogether
  while holding the paydown at its gold value — not for the swap the sentence describes.
- **evidence** recomputed on the swapped order: the paydown on the opening world is **150.00** (agrees);
  `meal_ext_period_recovery_amount` reads no load rows, so the recovery is still 85.05; at the
  reinstatement `balance_standing_usd = 164.75`, `value_loaded_1m = 150.00` →
  `applied_from_value_usd = 150.00`, and
  `result = RND(MX(0, 164.75 − 150.00 − 14.25 + 6.00 + 33.45), 2) = **39.95**`.
  Separately, 140.49 is reproduced exactly by `RND(MX(0, 249.80 − 134.51 − 14.25 + 6.00 + 33.45), 2)`,
  the "skip the recovery, hold the paydown at gold" run that `edge_load_bearing[1]` describes.
- **demonstrated consequence** the assertion the artifact offers as its proof of order uniqueness does not
  hold on recomputation. The conclusion survives (39.95 ≠ 55.44, so the order is still unique), but the
  evidence submitted for it is a figure from another run.
- **affected artifact** `tasks/0.json` `prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness`.
- **relation to previous revisions** first revision.

### F-8 — observation — the plan's automatic reload should have fired on this seed, and the rationale excuses it with a condition the base rule does not contain

- base `meal_load_and_refund_terms`: "Where the plan carries an automatic reload, it fires **once the
  balance falls to the reload threshold** printed against the plan and adds the reload amount printed
  against it, and it fires no more than once in a service day." The plan's
  `auto_reload_threshold_usd = 10.00`, `auto_reload_amount_usd = 25.00`; the seed's
  `meal_balance_usd = 8.75`, and no `account_load` row stands after 2026-01-20.
- `design_rationale` states: "the plan's automatic reload (threshold 10.00) has not fired **because no load
  has been made since the balance fell**" — a qualifying condition that appears nowhere in the base
  sentence, which triggers on the balance falling, not on a load being made.
- had it fired as base requires, `meal_balance_usd` would be 33.75 with a fresh `account_load` row inside
  the calendar month, changing `stored_value_credit_usd`, `reload_top_up_usd`, `value_loaded_1m` and all
  three scored figures. Recorded as an observation rather than a red light because no tool in this
  difficulty fires an automatic reload, so the solving agent reaches no second answer from it; the defect is
  in the seed and in the justification offered for it.
- affected artifact: `tasks/0.json` `initial_state.meal_accounts.bfc789e2-…` and `design_rationale`.

### F-9 — observations carried from `_difficulty.md`, with their effect on this world

- **CG-7** — `value_application_basis`' fall-through tier is unreachable at a reinstatement write; on this
  world the factor still bears weight through its two reachable rungs (46.69 under baseline vs 55.44).
- **CG-14** — `cafe_contracts.e1e83343-…` is seeded with the **employee's** `customer_id` although the
  schema defines that column as the client organisation holding the contract. The read still lands on one
  row and `find_cafe_contracts(customer_id="0f2296e6-…")` reaches it, so no second reading follows.
- **CG-16** — the account is `payroll_cycle: "biweekly"` while every `pay_period` on its own rows is a
  half-month label. The field is load-bearing: `recoverable_window_basis` takes rung 1 *because* the cycle
  is biweekly; on the semimonthly rung the same world gives `recoverable_balance_usd = 197.40` and a
  scored **94.40** instead of 85.05. The clash originates in `db_schema.json`'s single `pay_period` format
  for all four cycles, not in this difficulty's authoring.
- **CG-8**, **CG-9**, **CG-12**, **CG-13** — no effect demonstrable on this world.

## findings (round 2)

### R2-F-1 — `SOURCE-CHAIN RED` — the replacement load-bearing proof names two intermediates the ladder does not produce

- **symptom** `prerequisite_closure.edge_load_bearing[2].skipped_effect` now reads: "Skipping the
  employee's paydown leaves nothing loaded in the calendar month, so the value applied is the whole stored
  value standing, 18.40, **the working float of 25.00 takes the value settled to nothing**, and the charges
  carried forward become 119.43 instead of 39.98."
- **root cause** the sentence was rewritten for the new ladder but the float was read off the ladder's
  **first** rung rather than the rung this counterfactual world takes.
- **evidence** recomputed on "recovery posted, paydown skipped":
  `own_meal_count_1m` = 3 ≥ 1, `meal_balance_usd` = 18.40, `daily_spend_cap_usd` = 55.00. The ladder's
  first rung requires "the stored value standing is **above** the daily spending ceiling"; 18.40 ≤ 55.00,
  so the **second** rung applies — "the smallest single load the plan accepts",
  `P('min_load_usd')` = **5.00**. Then `value_settled_usd = MX(0.0, 18.40 − 5.00) = **13.40**`, not
  nothing, and `result = RND(MX(0, 155.40 − 13.40 − 22.57), 2) = 119.43`.
- **demonstrated consequence** the result figure is right, but two of the three intermediates the proof
  offers for it are false: the float is 5.00, not 25.00, and the value settled is 13.40, not nothing. A
  reader checking the edge against the charter finds the stated mechanism contradicted by the ladder.
  This is the same class as round-1 **F-6** ("the value applied from the account is 0.00 … 189.95"),
  recurring in the sentence written to replace it — the figure was recomputed, the reasoning around it was
  not.
- **affected artifact** `tasks/0.json` `prerequisite_closure.edge_load_bearing[2].skipped_effect`. The
  matching line of `design_rationale` ("edge C skipped -> … 39.98 -> 119.43") states only the figure and is
  correct.
- **relation to previous revisions** round-1 F-6 is closed on its original instance; this is its class
  recurring in the replacement text. Reported as closed-but-with-a-new-defect.

### N-2 demonstrated on this world — `SOURCE-POLICY RED`

Charter-global finding at `_difficulty.md` `# revision_2 / #### N-2`. On this world: the gold write settles
`value_settled_usd` = **92.85** against the arrears (155.40 − 92.85 − 22.57 = 39.98), while
`lift_meal_account_restriction_a306574a` updates only `status`, `restriction_start_date` and
`payroll_arrears_usd`. After the run `meal_balance_usd` stands at **136.25** — the 18.40 seeded plus the
whole 117.85 the employee paid in — so the 92.85 the policy has counted as settled is still spendable at
the till. The rule's own sentence draws the distinction it then fails to effect: the working float of 25.00
"stays on the account as the employee's own spendable value", which says nothing about the 92.85 unless the
92.85 leaves. The employee's 117.85 therefore both clears 92.85 of arrears and remains theirs.

### N-1 demonstrated on this world — `SOURCE-FACTOR RED`

Charter-global finding at `_difficulty.md` `# revision_2 / #### N-1`. On this world
`employer_pickup_base` takes rung 1 and returns `charges_accrued_1m` = **188.05**; rung 2 would return
`charges_accrued_3m` = **400.85**. The two rungs differ only in the aggregation window, which is what the
charter labels `method` in `value_application_basis` — a factor of this same policy — and in
`recoverable_window_basis` and `measured_balance_basis`, both used by this same task. The factor is
declared `effect: parameter`. It bears weight either way (62.55 under its baseline against a gold of
39.98); the defect is the label.

## findings (round 3)

No red light for this task. Three observations, all cited from `_difficulty.md` `# revision_3 / findings`
with their effect on this world:

- **N3-1** — `meal_ext_reinstatement_paydown` states that a guest meal accrues to payroll net of the
  surcharge, and this world follows it exactly (24.60 → 20.10, 22.70 → 18.20). The sentence does real work:
  it is why the paydown's 9.00 of guest surcharge is not the double charge round-1 **F-4** found. But the
  base event `meal_purchase_posted` maps the meal's own `amount_usd` onto the accrual, and the base policy
  that governs accrual is cited and superseded only in tree B's policy. No scored value differs for a
  solving agent, which reads the accrual rows rather than deriving them.
- **N3-2** — the lift → paydown gate now responds to `value_loaded_1m > 0`, not to the paydown's size, so a
  150.00 load and the gold 134.16 load both give 123.71. The edge still bears weight (133.64 vs 123.71) and
  the task carries three `value_input` edges against a floor of one.
- **N3-3** — the employee pays in 134.16 and none of it reduces what they owe; it lands as stored value
  they keep (`meal_balance_usd` 152.56) and buys an 8-point uplift in the employer's pickup. Declared by a
  sound `overwrite` and stated outright in the lift rule, so not a red light; recorded because the
  quantity is still called a paydown.
- **CG-8**, **CG-9**, **CG-14** — carried forward unchanged.

`short_tender_deferral` turns on how many overdraft charges fall in "the last three calendar months".
The world holds two: 2026-02-13 and 2026-03-09.

| reading of the window | overdrafts counted | tier | `deferred_recovery_usd` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| trailing three months from the clock (2025-12-18 → 2026-03-17) | 2 | rung 1, deep | **45.00** |
| the three completed named months, December–February | 1 (only 2026-02-13) | rung 2, light | **20.00** |
| the named months January–March | 2 | rung 1, deep | 45.00 |

A 25.00 swing in an input that feeds the first scored value directly. The round-3 rule sentence said only
"in the last three calendar months" and nothing in the charter chose between the readings, so the render
auditor's classification was correct.

**The repair closes it here.** The sentence now reads "…two or more overdraft charges have been raised on
it in the **three calendar months running back from the day the account is worked**", and the same
qualifier carries into `compute_basis.overdraft_count_3m`, into the ladder's `when` string and into
`baseline.rule`. Only the trailing reading survives, and it is the one the scored 83.85 rests on.

**The counting sentence is faithful on this world.** All 33 distinct dates in this ledger were tested at
every window length the charter uses here (1, 2, 3 and 12 months) under both readings the sentence admits:
**not one membership disagreement**, and none against the harness. The nearest thing to a boundary case is
the `account_load` of 2025-12-28, whose day-of-month is 28 — the last day that exists in every month — so
even February raises no question. The clock falls on the 17th, so no window edge lands on a 29th, 30th or
31st. See `_difficulty.md` **N4-1** for why the sentence is nonetheless not the harness's rule in general.

**No eligibility and no gate moved.** `meal_ext_period_recovery_amount`, `meal_ext_reinstatement_paydown`
and `meal_ext_restriction_lift_balance` carry no `eligibility` key, before or after; their `prerequisite`
and `overwrite` blocks are object-identical to round 3; the base eligibilities this task answers to
(`recoverable_state`, `loadable_state`, `restriction_state`) are in the frozen base section and were
re-verified as satisfied. Checks 4 and 5 are unchanged from `revision_3`: same three-step order on the same
world, every input a seeded record, a prior write, or the customer's immediate card payment.
